what_this_is: the DELPHI dev log: one entry per feature, each written three times, with every technical term clickable and every section collapsible.

views.skim: the single most surprising true thing, plus bullets that each carry a number
views.deep: the full entry: why it is fun, why it is science, what stays open regardless of data, and what is on disk
views.blog: narrative prose for a curious outsider, ending on the open question rather than a summary

framework.interpretation_is_mine: the DNA triad was named by the project lead and defined nowhere in the repository. This reading is an interpretation, recorded so it can be corrected. Grep confirms zero prior uses of Nous or Aletheia.

delphi.name: Delphi
delphi.gloss: the oracle. What could be built, and what would happen if it were.
delphi.what_it_does: proposes organisms, designs edits, simulates development, scores plausibility
delphi.its_characteristic_failure: fluency. An oracle is never short of an answer, and a design system will produce a cassette for any request put to it - including the two of our three worked requests that are not genome-editing problems at all.

nous.name: Nous
nous.gloss: intellect. What follows from what, independently of whether anyone has looked.
nous.what_it_does: states laws, proves theorems, checks that a conclusion follows from its premises
nous.its_characteristic_failure: vacuity, and its quieter cousin, proving the wrong statement soundly. A theorem with unsatisfiable hypotheses is true and says nothing; a theorem whose English gloss does not match its Lean passes every check this repository has.

aletheia.name: Aletheia
aletheia.gloss: ἀλήθεια - literally UN-concealment, un-forgetting. Truth as disclosure rather than as correspondence.
aletheia.what_it_does: measures against the world, records provenance, refuses, and says what is not known
aletheia.its_characteristic_failure: the false negative that looks like diligence - a check that reports clean because it could not find the field it was checking. This repository produced exactly that twice in one week.
aletheia.why_the_etymology_matters: the Greek word is privative: a-letheia, NOT-hidden, from lethe, forgetting. It is a better name for this layer than "truth" would be, because almost nothing here establishes that a claim is correct. What it does is stop things being concealed - a depicted mesh marked as depicted, a value marked not-established, a scorer measured against data it did not choose. The discipline is not correspondence, it is refusing to forget what a number was made of.

why_three.the_argument: each layer fails in a way the other two cannot see. Delphi cannot tell a good design from a fluent one. Nous cannot tell a sound proof from a relevant one. Aletheia cannot tell you what to build, only what is so. Run any one alone and the characteristic failure goes unnoticed.
why_three.the_worked_instance: the design scorer calls an animal whose dorsal fin begins past the end of its body TYPICAL, and ranks it above 87% of real fish. Delphi could not see it - the score is exactly what the model says. Nous could not see it either, until a registry law was read as a geometric constraint. It took Aletheia, in the form of a search over real specimens, to find an animal the other two layers agreed was ordinary.
why_three.the_asymmetry: the layers are not equal partners. Aletheia is the only one that can say NO on evidence, which is why most of the recent work lives there, and why a refusal is treated as a result rather than a failure to produce one.

goals.name: Agentic biomaterials
goals.note: team members were in the xenobot lab this week
goals.what_it_is: materials that behave: structures made of living cells that move, repair and act, rather than materials that merely have properties.
goals.why_it_sharpens_the_work: a xenobot is the cleanest counterexample to the assumption this pipeline is built on. It is an organism assembled from cells WITHOUT EDITING A GENOME - the design acts on arrangement, adhesion and geometry, and the genome goes along unchanged. Our design surface is an edit list against a reference assembly, which cannot express "take these cells and put them there". The three worked requests already showed one case where the genome was the wrong target; this is a whole class where it is.
goals.what_we_would_have_to_build: a design representation whose primitive is a cell arrangement rather than a sequence edit. .life is closer to this than .organism is - it already carries per-cell position, radius and neighbour-dependent geometry - but nothing in the pipeline can currently propose an arrangement.
goals.the_open_question: what is the unit of agency? A xenobot does things no cell in it does. Whether that is emergence worth a new vocabulary or just mechanics at a larger scale is not settled by watching more of them.

goals.name: Evolutionary biology, and reverse-engineering biological laws and constraints
goals.what_it_is: recovering the constraints that make some organisms possible and others not - and stating them precisely enough to be wrong.
goals.why_it_sharpens_the_work: this is what the 62-law registry IS, and the benchmarks measured how far it reaches. The result is sobering and useful: only 1 of 48 theorem-carrying laws is expressible on the ten body-ratio traits, because the registry speaks in quantities those traits do not carry - two sizes, a population, a power budget, a genotype. A law you cannot evaluate on your data is not yet a constraint on your design.
goals.what_we_would_have_to_build: the missing direction. Everything so far states a law and checks it; nothing INFERS one from data. Reverse-engineering means going from the cloud of real organisms to the boundary of it, and the adversarial search is the first thing here that touches that boundary from the outside.
goals.the_open_question: is a biological "law" a constraint, a regularity, or a habit? Allometric exponents hold until they do not. More measurements sharpen the exponent without telling you whether an exception refutes the law or merely bounds it.

goals.name: Other open biological questions, including origins of life
goals.what_it_is: the questions that are open for reasons other than insufficient effort.
goals.why_it_sharpens_the_work: origins of life is the hardest case of the thing this whole discipline keeps running into: a question where the evidence is gone. Every other item here can in principle be settled by a measurement. That one cannot, because the event left almost no record and the record it left has been overwritten by four billion years of descendants. It is the limiting case of aletheia as UN-forgetting - the thing was not hidden, it was forgotten, and no instrument recovers it.
goals.what_we_would_have_to_build: the honest version is not a simulation of abiogenesis. It is a machine-checkable account of what each proposed route REQUIRES - which is the shape the law registry already has, and the shape the lean-open-problems triage says is worth having: a system that can derive a contradiction from its own accepted premises plus a measurement.
goals.the_open_question: what would count as settling it? A demonstration that life CAN arise a particular way is not a demonstration that it DID. That gap is logical, not empirical, and it will survive any amount of laboratory success.

how_goals_meet_the_triad.the_pattern: each goal is dominated by a different layer, which is some evidence the triad is carving at joints rather than being imposed. Biomaterials is a generation problem, law-recovery an inference problem, and origins an evidence problem.
how_goals_meet_the_triad.the_uncomfortable_implication: the pipeline as built is strongest at the layer the goals need least. Delphi will happily produce a cassette for any request; two of the three worked requests did not need one, and an entire goal - agentic biomaterials - does not involve editing a genome at all.

entries.title: .life — an organism's whole trajectory, in time
entries.why_fun: A file format is the most durable thing you can build. .stl outlived every program that made one, because it was simple enough to be obvious and specific enough to be useful. The idea that a designed organism could have an extension - that you could double-click a creature - is a good enough idea on its own that it is worth seeing whether it survives contact with the biology.
entries.why_science: A .organism describes a design AT REST; stages are metadata. That is the wrong shape for the thing actually being designed, which is a trajectory. And the difference is not cosmetic: A SNAPSHOT CANNOT BE WRONG ABOUT A TRAJECTORY - it has nothing to be wrong with. Make time the primary axis and the file starts making claims that can be FALSE - that this cell count follows that one, that this stiffness falls as that lineage separates - which is what makes them worth storing.

open_questions.q: When is a simulated organism "the same organism" as the design it came from?
open_questions.why_data_will_not_settle_it: identity over time is a definitional boundary, not a measurement. A trajectory that diverges from its design at stage 4 is either a failed instance of that design or a different design, and no amount of imaging decides which. The file has to pick a convention and say so.

open_questions.q: What is the right granularity for a stage?
open_questions.why_data_will_not_settle_it: development is continuous and staging is a human imposition on it. Carnegie stages are defined by morphology precisely because age does not work, and the cost is that a stage is a RANGE of days that overlaps its neighbours. Finer imaging gives you more frames, not a principled stage boundary.

open_questions.q: Should a format be able to represent an organism that cannot exist?
open_questions.why_data_will_not_settle_it: this is a design choice with real consequences either way. Forbid it and you cannot write down a hypothesis; allow it and the file cannot be trusted as a record. .life allows it and requires it to be marked, which is a third answer and not obviously the right one.

files: the format: FORMAT tag, CHANNELS, STAGE_REQUIRED, TIME_UNITS, REFUSALS, the two geometry-provenance axes, COORDINATE_CONVENTIONS
the builder. Requires provenance AT CONSTRUCTION and throws without it - 12 refusals verified firing
the validator: refused / degraded / ok, plus channelCoverage and provenanceCensus
binary STL export, provenance burned into the 80-byte header
genome export, provenance forced into every description line
genetic and phenotypic distance, returned separately and never summed
the Carnegie-stage layer, ordinal and refusing arithmetic
the worked example, 5 stages and 31 cells
how_file_level.what_is_packed_in: A .life is JSON with four required blocks. `identity` says what animal this is. `genome` is an EDIT-LIST against a named reference assembly - kilobytes rather than hundreds of megabytes, and it states what the design IS rather than what it resembles. `timeline.stages[]` is the spine: each stage pins itself with a time, a TIME UNIT and a TEMPERATURE (development rate is temperature-dependent, so a stage time without one is not a stage), and carries `geometry` (per-cell centre, radius, surface area, EXPOSED surface area, curvature) plus a `phenotype` map. Each cell may carry channels: transcriptome (with an in_situ flag), mechanics, geometry, lineage, signalling. And `not_established` is required - a file that lists nothing it does not know is making the strongest possible claim by omission.
how_file_level.the_detail_that_matters: EVERY VALUE CARRIES A KIND AND A SCOPE. The kinds are measured, measured-secondhand, borrowed, derived, calibrated, assumed, depicted. An `unknown` carries no value at all - that rule exists because a value of the shape {v: 0.31, unknown: true} slipped past every provenance check in the .organism reader. The census line that falls out is the most useful line in the file: the worked example is 10 measured-secondhand / 5 assumed / 5 depicted / 5 derived / 5 not-established, and NONE measured by us.

real_numbers: 5 stages, 31 cells, 25 phenotype values in the worked example
geometry present on 31 of 31 cells, MEASURED ON 0
transcriptome and mechanics present on 0 of 31 cells
226 tests across the format modules, 0 survive their own fault
what_went_wrong: The spec required `elastic_modulus_Pa` as a field name, following an abstract that turned out to be a STALE v1 deposit. The authors had retreated to "relative compliance". A field name can impose a unit the measurement does not have - requiring pascals does not make the data a modulus, it makes the file lie in a way no reader can detect.

read.mjs stringified `{what, answer}` entries to "[object Object]", so it reported the example missing all four required disclosures while the example answered all four verbatim. A false negative in the honesty check is worse than no check.

entries.title: Benchmarks — the state of the system as measured, not as described
entries.why_fun: There is a particular pleasure in finding out that something you built does not work, before someone else does. It is also the only move in this whole field that is guaranteed to teach you something: a benchmark that confirms what you believed is a wasted afternoon, and one that does not is the best day of the month.
entries.why_science: "61 laws registered, 73 Lean-checked theorems" and "AUC 0.89" are PRODUCTIVITY figures. They measure how much was built and they cannot come out badly. A benchmark has to be able to come out badly, which means the answer has to come from somewhere the system does not control. Three of the four here did come out badly, which is the point.

open_questions.q: Does a plausibility score ever constitute evidence of viability?
open_questions.why_data_will_not_settle_it: this is a category question, not an empirical one. A Mahalanobis distance measures how unusual a vector is under a fitted distribution. More data makes the distribution better estimated; it does not turn "unusual" into "impossible". We demonstrated the gap - an animal whose dorsal fin starts past its tail scores more typical than 87% of real fish - but the gap is structural and would survive a perfect model.

open_questions.q: What should a benchmark do when the ground truth is itself a model?
open_questions.why_data_will_not_settle_it: CRISPRscan reaches rho 0.269 on data from the study that fitted it. That is an upper bound, not an estimate, and the only fix is independent data - but "independent" is a judgement about provenance and shared assumptions, not a quantity you can measure.

open_questions.q: Is soundness ever evidence of relevance?
open_questions.why_data_will_not_settle_it: the Lean layer proves things correctly. Whether the things proved are the things that matter to a design is a question about the choice of formalisation, and no proof assistant has an opinion about it.

files: the index: the four results, the five properties, and the two predictions that came out wrong
the guide score against 307 measured zebrafish sgRNAs; CRISPRscan reimplemented and verified
non-vacuity, and mutation testing with the three-way kill classification
the decoy ladder, the adversarial search, and laws.mjs deriving constraints from the registry
how_file_level.what_is_packed_in: Each directory is self-contained: a module holding the method, a `run.mjs` producing a `results.json`, a `test.mjs` taking `--fail-once`, and a README stating the result and what it does NOT cover. `crispr-ontarget/SOURCES.md` rebuilds the ground truth in three curls; the ground truth itself is copyrighted and is not redistributed.
how_file_level.the_detail_that_matters: The `--fail-once` discipline: the harness injects ONE fault per assertion and requires that the assertion notices. AN ASSERTION THAT SURVIVES ITS OWN FAULT IS REPORTED AS A FAILURE, because it was not testing anything. Across every suite in this work: 0 survivors.

real_numbers: the guide score we rank by: rho = -0.037, CI [-0.149, 0.073] - includes zero
CRISPRscan layout DERIVED by reproducing 25 published scores exactly, max difference 0.0000
design AUC: 0.891 on shuffled decoys, 0.536 on real fish nudged a quarter of a standard deviation
an anatomically impossible animal at q = 0.347, more typical than 4,068 of 4,673 real fish
48/48 laws with a theorem carry a machine-checked non-vacuity witness
only 1 of 48 theorem-carrying laws is expressible on the ten trait ratios
what_went_wrong: A first CRISPRscan alignment gave a plausible rho = 0.75 at the WRONG offset - pure misalignment artefact, because reverse-complementing a window flips its flanks with it. It would have shipped.

A written prediction that correlation-preserving decoys would score 0.5 "by construction" came out at 0.663, because the fitted Gaussian is OVERDISPERSED relative to real fish. The wrong prediction was more informative than the right one would have been.

entries.title: The fifth property: a benchmark needs a control
entries.why_fun: Every single control built this week caught MY work rather than the system's. That is a slightly humbling pattern and a very reassuring one: it means the controls are load-bearing rather than decorative, which is not true of most tests.
entries.why_science: A benchmark must take its answer from outside the system, be able to fail, state its scope, and be reproducible. Those four are standard. The fifth is not, and it is the one that actually bit: without a control you cannot distinguish "the system failed" from "my harness cannot tell".

open_questions.q: How do you control a control?
open_questions.why_data_will_not_settle_it: the regress is real. The Lean control was a weakened mutant that must survive; it came back UNPROVEN, revealing the harness was too weak. But that only worked because I knew independently that the weakened statement was true. At some point a human judgement terminates the chain, and no amount of automation removes that point - it only moves it.

open_questions.q: When a plausible constraint fails on real data, is the constraint wrong or the data?
open_questions.why_data_will_not_settle_it: one "preanal <= 1 SL" violator is almost certainly a measurement artefact. But overruling a control because the violator looks wrong is exactly the move the control exists to prevent, so it stands. Which way to resolve this is a methodological commitment, not a finding.

files: REJECTED carries each failed candidate WITH its measured rate, so the mistake cannot be repeated quietly
verifyAgainstReal() returns counts, not booleans; cleared() admits only rate exactly 1.0
is_control marks the mutant that MUST survive
mayGate() refuses in code anything below 1.0 support
how_file_level.what_is_packed_in: A rejected constraint is not deleted. It is kept with the share of real specimens that satisfy it and a `why_not` - so the file records the near-miss rather than only the survivor.
how_file_level.the_detail_that_matters: The rule is enforced in code, not in a comment: a constraint may gate ONLY when its recorded support over a real sample is exactly 1. A gate that rejects real fish is worse than no gate.

real_numbers: "the pectoral fin sits behind the head" is FALSE for 39% of real fish - 4,673 specimens checked
the real-specimen control rejected 4 of 8 candidates in one module and 7 of 13 in another
a plausible-sounding anatomical containment is about as likely to be wrong as right
the gate refuses 0 of 4,673 real specimens, which is the only property that makes it deployable
what_went_wrong: I ran the holdout leak gate and git commit in one && chain, so a flagged leak did not block the commit. A GATE CHAINED BEHIND THE ACTION IT GUARDS IS NOT A GATE.
A Lean mutant was aimed the wrong way: widening a disjunct WEAKENS a conclusion, so the "false" mutant stayed true. Lean said so precisely - the attempted counterexample was inside the measured band.

entries.title: Analogy mapping — homology is not function
entries.why_fun: The question "is this the same thing as that?" is the oldest question in comparative biology and it is still not mechanised. Watching agents fan out over twenty genomes to answer it, and then watching most of the answers get thrown out, is the most honest demo this project has.
entries.why_science: DELPHI designs by borrowing a structure from one species into another, which requires deciding when a gene in A is the FUNCTIONAL ANALOGUE of one in B. The pipeline treated orthology as if it answered this. It does not. Homology is shared ancestry; analogy is shared function without it. An ortholog can have diverged entirely, a one-to-many orthologue is not an equivalent of anything, and the convergent cases a design programme most cares about have no orthology at all.

open_questions.q: What makes two structures "the same structure"?
open_questions.why_data_will_not_settle_it: homology is a claim about history, and history is not directly observable. Sequence, position, development and expression are all correlates, and they disagree - a structure can be positionally homologous and developmentally novel. There is no measurement that returns "same", only measurements that return "similar in this respect".

open_questions.q: How should incommensurable evidence kinds be weighed against each other?
open_questions.why_data_will_not_settle_it: rescue experiments, synteny, expression similarity and domain architecture are different kinds of evidence, not different amounts of one kind. Collapsing them into a single confidence number requires weights, and the weights are a modelling choice that propagates into every downstream decision. More data makes each kind better measured and does not make them commensurable.

open_questions.q: Is "no orthologue found" ever evidence of absence?
open_questions.why_data_will_not_settle_it: searching one database is not searching. The strength of a negative depends on the coverage and sensitivity of what was searched, which is a judgement about the search, not a result of it.

files: live NCBI Datasets v2, Ensembl REST and E-utilities, with on-disk caching to C:/Temp and real rate limiting
the curated species inventory, each entry stating WHY it is a reference and verified to resolve
EVIDENCE_KINDS, the classifier, and the refusals
real Gotoh affine-gap Needleman-Wunsch and Smith-Waterman, BLOSUM62, and the cassette layout
the tree, divergence ranges, and phenome correspondence classes
assembles the animation data and degrades rather than failing
how_file_level.what_is_packed_in: Nothing in here caches into the repository. Genome responses go to C:/Temp/delphi-genome-cache/ keyed by a hash of the URL, because the repo already has a rule against committing large data and a genome is the canonical violation of it. Every fetch distinguishes three outcomes that are usually collapsed: the API said no, the API failed, and we did not ask.
how_file_level.the_detail_that_matters: THE TELEOST PROBLEM. The teleost genome duplication means many zebrafish genes are duplicate pairs that SPLIT the ancestral function, so a single mammalian gene maps to two fish genes each doing part of the job. A mapping that picks one and calls it "the" orthologue is wrong in a way that shows up as a failed experiment. We have a live instance: kcnk5b and its paralog kcnk5a.

entries.title: Three requests that fail in three different ways
entries.why_fun: A glowing fly, a higher-protein worm, and a cow that burps less. They sound like three versions of the same request and they are not even the same KIND of request, which is the most useful thing about the set.
entries.why_science: Only one of the three is a genome-editing problem in the shape the pipeline assumes. One is not a mapping problem - the function is ADDED, not transferred, and no orthologue exists or is needed. One is polygenic and not a single edit. And one is not about the named organism at all: enteric methane is produced by rumen archaea, and the cow genome encodes no methanogenesis pathway. A system that silently produced a cassette for all three would be wrong three times over.

open_questions.q: Where does an organism end and its microbiome begin?
open_questions.why_data_will_not_settle_it: the methane case forces this. If the trait of interest is produced by an associated community, is the "designed organism" the cow, the holobiont, or the archaea? Sequencing everything does not answer it - the boundary is a choice about what counts as the unit being engineered.

open_questions.q: What does the person asking for a glowing fly actually want?
open_questions.why_data_will_not_settle_it: fluorescence needs excitation light, so a GFP fly does NOT glow in the dark; bioluminescence needs a luciferase AND a substrate the fly cannot make. Which one was meant is a fact about the asker, not about the fly, and it changes the entire design.

methane yield has non-zero heritability through host effects on the rumen environment. That makes it a selection target. Whether any identified locus is an EDIT target is a different claim, and a heritability estimate - however precise - does not contain it.

files: CASES[] with verdict, is_the_target_organism_the_right_one, CRISPR_RELEVANCE and real citations
the generated animation data, one entry per case, eight stages each
the animation: canvas scene, stage rail, and refusals drawn across the whole frame
how_file_level.what_is_packed_in: Each case carries the request as the lead phrased it, what is ACTUALLY being asked, the target organism and whether it is the right one, the analogy class, what would have to be measured, a verdict from a closed vocabulary, how it could fail, and sources with real DOIs - null and flagged where unverified, because a fabricated DOI is worse than none.
how_file_level.the_detail_that_matters: CRISPR_RELEVANCE asks, per case, whether a cassette is even the right tool. For the fly the classic tool is transgenesis rather than knock-in; for the cow it is beside the point entirely. A design system that answers "CRISPR cassette" to every request is a hammer.

real_numbers: the storyboard asserts at least one case refuses before reaching a cassette - a storyboard where everything succeeds is a bug in the storyboard
and asserts not everything refuses, since showing nothing working is the opposite failure

entries.title: Ecology — the quantity that decides survival is not the one the design optimises
entries.why_fun: The result is genuinely counterintuitive and takes two lines of arithmetic: a design that grows 67% faster still loses. You can show that to anyone in thirty seconds and it changes how they think about what "better" means.
entries.why_science: A design is not released into an empty world. Tilman's R* rule says that with one limiting resource at steady state, the species with the lowest R* = Ks*D/(mu_max - D) competitively EXCLUDES the others - not "does better", excludes. R* turns on affinity at least as much as on rate, and a design optimised for maximum growth rate is not thereby safe. It is often the opposite, because the engineered pathway costs low-substrate performance.

open_questions.q: Is R* the right frame for a release at all?
open_questions.why_data_will_not_settle_it: R* describes steady state in a well-mixed system. Soil is neither. The honest answer may be that it is the BEST CASE for the design - if it loses here it loses everywhere - but whether that framing is appropriate is a judgement about model applicability, not a measurement.

open_questions.q: If low-substrate affinity decides survival and we optimise rate, is the design objective wrong?
open_questions.why_data_will_not_settle_it: that is a question for whoever sets the objective. The model can say which quantity decides the outcome; it cannot say which outcome you should want.

files: Monod growth, R*, compete(), assessDesign() and WHAT_R_STAR_IGNORES
two-resource theory: ZNGIs for essential and substitutable resources, consumption vectors, mutual invasibility
how_file_level.what_is_packed_in: Three numbers per organism settle the single-resource question: mu_max, Ks, and the loss rate D of the environment entered. The module REFUSES to assess any design lacking measured mu_max and Ks, and returns the bar plus the three measurements that would settle it, because a competition outcome computed from invented growth constants looks exactly like one computed from measurements.
how_file_level.the_detail_that_matters: The two-resource module corrected the one-resource module. WHAT_R_STAR_IGNORES said two resources make the single-resource conclusion "lapse entirely". It does not - it GENERALISES. A species with the lower R* on both resources excludes the other outright at every supply point. It lapses only where the isoclines cross, which is where there is a real trade-off.

real_numbers: design mu_max 0.5 / Ks 1.0 -> R* 0.25 LOSES to incumbent mu_max 0.3 / Ks 0.1 -> R* 0.05
the design grows 67% faster and would need to be 5x better to win
no designed organism in this repository has a measured mu_max or Ks, so every assessment refuses
reverse ONLY the consumption vectors, leave all four R* identical, and stable coexistence flips to founder-control

entries.title: The holdout — a clade nobody is allowed to mention
entries.why_fun: There is something genuinely strange about working on a comparative-biology project where one entire class of animals is unspeakable. It shapes the code in visible ways: a tree-of-life module has to actively avoid reaching for it, and a survey of registry laws had to redact two identifiers and fill them in at runtime instead.
entries.why_science: A held-out evaluation set is only held out if nothing leaks into the work. Not the species names, not the clade, not a claim id whose organisms all belong to it - because any of those tells a later reader what the evaluation is about, and a system tuned against a leaked holdout has measured itself.

open_questions.q: How much can leak before a holdout stops being one?
open_questions.why_data_will_not_settle_it: there is no measurement of "how much information about the evaluation entered the design". A leak check counts tokens; it cannot count influence. The honest position is that a leaked holdout is compromised and you cannot quantify by how much.

how_file_level.path: holdout/ (owned by another thread) and every module that touches taxa
files: scans a path for held-out taxa and for claim ids whose organisms are all held out
two registry rows take their law_id from the registry AT RUNTIME so the identifiers never appear in source
one problem WITHDRAWN rather than written, with a comment saying why the count is 14 and not 15
how_file_level.what_is_packed_in: The gate reports leaks and warnings separately and exits non-zero on a leak. The rule here is that rulings belong to the holdout thread: a leak is fixed by REDACTION, never by adding an allowlist entry, because allowlisting is a judgement about scope that is not mine to make.
how_file_level.the_detail_that_matters: check-leaks does not scan .html or .glb files, so those are grepped by hand. A gate with a documented blind spot is only as good as the habit that covers it.

real_numbers: two leaks reached a commit this week; both were redacted rather than allowlisted
one survey keeps all 62 registry rows while naming only 60 of them
what_went_wrong: A `git add <directory>` swept in a half-written module from a running agent, and separately a leak gate chained with && behind the commit it guarded did not block it. Both are the same root cause: a broad command staging whatever happens to be there.

the_four_questions: what stays open regardless of data
how_to_read_this.the_open_questions_rule: an entry under open_questions must be one where MORE MEASUREMENT IS NOT THE KIND OF THING THAT WOULD HELP. "We have not measured it yet" is not an open question in this sense, it is a task. The ones listed are definitional boundaries, modelling choices and category questions - and they are the part of the work most likely to still be interesting in ten years.
how_to_read_this.what_went_wrong_is_not_optional: every entry carries its mistakes. A dev log that records only what worked is a changelog with better typography, and the failures here were more instructive than the successes - a wrong prediction about decoy AUC taught more than a right one would have.
